title: Her Twins Read the Divorce Papers in German. Her Husband Said, 'I'll Get You a Job Cleaning Supermarkets.' Celina Jaitly Is Done Being Quiet.
excerpt: In a raw, devastating interview, the former Miss India reveals the full scope of her cross-border divorce nightmare — the ₹20 crore she says she lost, the custody battle she's fighting across two countries, and the one Bollywood friend who never left her side.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Celina Jaitly reveals her painful divorce experience, including a custody battle across two countries.
  • She claims to have lost ₹20 crore in assets during her marriage to Peter Haag.
  • Her twins read the divorce papers in German, highlighting the emotional toll of the situation.
  • Bollywood actress Preity Zinta has been a crucial support during Celina's difficult times.
  • Celina is making a comeback after 15 years, portraying Sister Nivedita in an upcoming biopic.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=RV-J8XsgKVw Celina Jaitly did not plan to tell the world about her marriage. The world found out anyway, and now she is telling it on her own terms — with a kind of clarity that only comes from having nothing left to protect. In a series of interviews with India Today and NDTV over the past week, the former Miss India Universe and *No Entry* star has laid bare the full, bruising story of her divorce from Austrian businessman Peter Haag. The details are specific, granular, and difficult to hear. They are also the kind of details that thousands of Indian women living abroad will recognise instantly. Start with the papers. Celina says she was taken to a post office in Austria, under the pretext of collecting a wedding anniversary gift, and handed a thick legal document instead. The papers were in German — not conversational German, but dense legal terminology she could not parse. Her husband, she alleges, refused to translate. So her twins did. Winston and Viraaj, who attend a German-medium school, sat down with their mother and read the divorce petition aloud. "I think this will be one of the most heartbreaking aspects of this whole divorce," Celina told India Today. "After 15 years of marriage, even if you have to separate, you cannot separate amicably just because you are eyeing someone's hard-earned money and assets." ![Preity Zinta — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/ef/Preity_Zinta_by_Ash_Gupta.jpg) > **"And that is what my biggest heartache is." She claims she was made to transfer personal properties worth around ₹20 crore during the marriage and was left with nothing after the separation."** The notice, she says, alleged she was not meeting her husband's needs and cited an irretrievable breakdown of the marriage. "I thought it was a joke," she said. It was not a joke. What followed, according to Celina, was a proposal she sent to Haag's lawyers requesting the return of her assets and continuation of joint custody. The response, she alleges, was an offer to help her find employment. "I was told, 'I will get you a job as a cleaner in a supermarket,'" she said. For a woman who was once one of Bollywood's most visible faces — four Miss India titles, a string of commercial hits, a decade-long career — the suggestion carried a particular sting. > "All the love, all the care, all the promises of togetherness, the children, the deaths, the births — everything boiled down to an asset at the end of the day. And that is what my biggest heartache is." She claims she was made to transfer personal properties worth around ₹20 crore during the marriage and was left with nothing after the separation. Haag and his father have denied all allegations and issued legal notices accusing her of defamation. ## The One Phone Call That Changed Everything When NDTV asked whether anyone from Bollywood had reached out, Celina did not hesitate. "My biggest supporter was Preity Zinta." She described Preity as "a fellow Fauji kid" — both women grew up in Indian military families, a bond that apparently runs deeper than industry friendships. "She is a very strong, dependable human being. She has been through a lot herself and she is a self-made woman as well." What Preity did, according to Celina, was simple and enormous: she showed up. "Preity stood by me like a rock in my darkest time when I couldn't even get out of my house. She is the one who even pushed me to come out into the limelight and think of my craft and embrace my craft." The isolation Celina describes is the part of this story that will land hardest with diaspora readers. "It's not that I came here and I could go to mum and dad and cry on their laps," she said. "I really did not know whom I could open up to, whom I could talk to." This is the unspoken reality of cross-border marriage for Indian women: when it works, you have built a life. When it breaks, you are alone in a foreign legal system, in a language you don't fully command, with your family a continent away and your children caught in the middle. ## The Comeback Nobody Expected And yet Celina Jaitly is not retreating. She is returning to the screen after **15 years** with what may be the most symbolically loaded role imaginable: **Sister Nivedita**, the Irish-born disciple of Swami Vivekananda who left her homeland and devoted her entire life to India. Directed by National Award-winning filmmaker Ram Kamal Mukherjee, the biopic will shoot across Mumbai, Kolkata, London, and Ireland. Celina says the connection is older than the film. As a child, when her father was posted in Binaguri, West Bengal, she would visit Roy Villa in Darjeeling — the place where Sister Nivedita spent her final days. "I had no idea that one day, far in the future, I would be the chosen one," she said. "Portraying Sister Nivedita feels less like a role and more like answering a calling." The parallels are almost too neat: a woman who crossed borders for love, who found herself unmade by the crossing, now playing a woman who crossed borders for faith and was remade by it. Whether the film delivers on that promise is a question for later. For now, the casting feels like a statement. Celina Jaitly married Peter Haag in 2010. They had twin sons in 2012 and a third son, Arthur, in 2017. She has filed an FIR in Mumbai under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act. The case is ongoing. Haag's family has denied all allegations.
Celina's Journey Back to the Screen
›Returning to acting after 15 years.
›Portraying Sister Nivedita, a significant role.
›Film directed by National Award-winning filmmaker.
›Shooting locations include Mumbai, Kolkata, London, and Ireland.
What is not in dispute is the advice she is now giving every Indian woman who will listen: "Please do a prenup if you have assets of your own. Please do a prenup before marrying. Keep your assets separate always." It is the kind of sentence that sounds like legal counsel. Coming from Celina Jaitly, it sounds like a scar.
